questions.q: In robot-centric driving, "forward" on the stick means...
questions.correct: Whichever way the robot is currently pointing
wrong: Always straight away from the driver's station
Always toward whichever wall is nearest
The direction the robot first started in
questions.explain: Robot-centric ties forward to the robot's own facing. When the robot spins, "forward" spins too — which gets confusing for the driver.

questions.q: In field-centric driving, "forward" on the stick means...
questions.correct: Always away from the driver, no matter the facing
wrong: Whatever way the robot happens to be pointing
Toward whichever field wall is the closest
The direction the robot's intake is facing
questions.explain: Field-centric keeps forward fixed to the field (away from the driver) no matter which way the robot faces. Push up and it goes away from you, always.

questions.q: Why do you need to translate the driver's request?
questions.correct: The wheels only understand the robot's own frame
wrong: The battery only supplies power in one frame
The gamepad reports numbers that are too large
The rules require a translation step first
questions.explain: Wheels think in robot-forward, but the driver commands field-forward. You rotate the request into robot-language before the mecanum mix uses it.

questions.q: The translation from field to robot frame is a...
wrong: Multiplication by the battery voltage
Reversal of the two left motors
Reset of the wheel encoder counts
questions.explain: If the robot is turned by some heading, its forward differs from the driver's by that same angle. Rotating the request by the heading lines them up.

wrong: Math.max and Math.min
Math.abs and Math.round
Math.hypot and Math.pow
questions.explain: cos and sin rotate the request. Think of them as the shadows of a direction arrow — how far it reaches across (cos) and up (sin).

questions.q: You rotate the request by which angle?
questions.correct: Negative heading, to un-turn the request
wrong: Positive heading, to add the turn again
Double the heading, to over-rotate it
Zero, so nothing actually rotates at all
questions.explain: You rotate by −heading to "un-turn" the driver's request back into robot-frame. Using +heading rotates the wrong way and steering breaks.

questions.correct: How far the arrow reaches across (horizontal)
wrong: How far the arrow reaches up (vertical)
The total length of the arrow itself
The battery voltage at that exact moment
questions.explain: cos is the horizontal shadow of a direction arrow (its reach across), and sin is the vertical shadow (its reach up). Together they rotate a vector.

questions.q: Before field-centric works well, you should...
questions.correct: Reset the heading to 0 at the match start
wrong: Reverse both of the left drive motors
Disable the IMU sensor entirely first
Set every wheel power to a full 1.0
questions.explain: Reset heading (often with the right bumper) so the robot's current facing counts as forward. Otherwise "forward" points wherever it started, which may be wrong.

questions.q: After rotating the request, the new values...
questions.correct: Flow into the same mecanum mix as before
wrong: Go straight to the tank drive formula
Get printed to telemetry and thrown away
Reverse the robot's turning direction
questions.explain: The rotated forward/strafe feed the exact same mecanum mixing math. The wheels never know a rotation happened — they just get robot-frame numbers.

questions.q: The two "forwards" in this lesson are...
questions.correct: The robot's forward and the driver's forward
wrong: The left motor's and the right motor's forward
The intake's forward and the shooter's forward
The battery's forward and the hub's forward
questions.explain: There's robot-forward (spins with the robot) and field/driver-forward (never changes). Field-centric keeps the stick tied to the driver's forward.

questions.q: Where does the heading come from?
wrong: The battery's charge level
The gamepad's A button
The telemetry update call
questions.explain: You read heading from the IMU in radians (getYaw), then rotate the drive request by −heading. Radians because cos and sin expect them.

questions.q: A wrong sign on the heading causes...
questions.correct: The rotation to go the wrong way
wrong: The battery to drain much faster
The telemetry to stop updating
The intake to run in reverse
questions.explain: Using +heading instead of −heading rotates the request the wrong direction, so field-centric steers backward. The minus "un-turns" it correctly.

questions.q: Why does the driver prefer field-centric when the robot spins?
questions.correct: Forward stays put, so driving stays intuitive
wrong: The robot drives twice as fast when spinning
The motors use far less of the battery power
The robot can never tip over while spinning
questions.explain: With field-centric, "up" on the stick always means away from the driver even as the robot rotates — so a spinning robot is still easy to control.

questions.correct: How far the arrow reaches up (vertical)
wrong: How far the arrow reaches across (horizontal)
The battery's current voltage reading
The number of encoder ticks counted
questions.explain: sin is the vertical shadow of a direction arrow (its reach up); cos is the horizontal shadow. The pair rotates the driver's request vector.

questions.q: After the rotation math, the wheels...
wrong: Must be rewired for each heading
Reverse their direction every loop
Ignore the driver's request entirely
questions.explain: The rotation happens before the mix, so the wheels just receive normal robot-frame drive/strafe numbers. They behave exactly as in plain mecanum.
